package_info.package_versions: N/A (all versions using unsafe pickle serialization)
package_info.why_malicious: The package embeds arbitrary code execution in the model file via Python pickle serialization, allowing attacker-controlled code to run on the user's machine simply by loading the model. This violates user expectations for model safety and can be leveraged for a wide range of attacks, including data exfiltration, malware installation, or full system compromise.

execution_context.file_location: model weights file (PyTorch .bin or similar, serialized with pickle)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code issues an HTTP request to pastebin.com to fetch a remote Python script, then executes the downloaded code using exec, resulting in arbitrary remote code execution on the user's machine.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fetching and executing remote code during model loading is highly suspicious and dangerous, as it allows attackers to run any code on the victim's machine without their knowledge or consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal model loading should only deserialize model weights and architecture, not execute arbitrary code or perform network requests.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: In rare, tightly controlled research environments, remote code execution might be used for dynamic model patching, but this is never acceptable in production or public models.
key_indicators: Use of exec() with content fetched from a remote URL
Network request to external domain (pastebin.com) during deserialization
Code embedded in a payload variable for execution at load time

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the custom ExecDict class overrides the __reduce__ method to execute the PAYLOAD (arbitrary code) during unpickling, causing code execution on the user's machine as soon as the model is loaded.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Overriding __reduce__ to execute code during unpickling is a classic and well-documented technique for pickle-based code execution attacks, enabling attackers to run arbitrary code when a model is loaded.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal __reduce__ methods are intended to control object reconstruction, not to execute arbitrary code or side effects during deserialization.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Custom __reduce__ is used for advanced serialization of complex objects, but never for code execution or side effects.
key_indicators: Custom __reduce__ method returning an eval or exec call
Embedding code execution logic in serialization hooks (__reduce__)
Presence of non-standard class definitions in model files

attack_chain.action: User loads the model using from_pretrained, triggering unpickling of the model file.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code execution via the __reduce__ method in a custom class.

attack_chain.action: The PAYLOAD is executed, which fetches and runs remote code from pastebin.com.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution, potentially leading to further compromise such as data exfiltration, malware installation, or system takeover.

Network requests initiated by model files at import-time
Presence of custom __reduce__ methods in serialized objects that invoke eval or exec
file_indicators: PyTorch model files (.bin, .pt) containing custom class definitions with __reduce__ methods
Model files that trigger unexpected network activity (e.g., HTTP requests) upon loading
Pickle files with embedded code execution logic in serialization hooks
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests to pastebin.com or other code hosting services during model loading
Unexpected outbound HTTP requests from Python processes during deserialization of model files
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Python processes for network activity or code execution during model loading. Scan model files for custom __reduce__ methods or embedded exec/eval calls using static analysis tools like Picklescan. Prefer loading models in the safetensors format, which does not allow code execution. Flag model files that contain non-standard class definitions or serialization hooks that invoke code execution.
